title: "Programme Overview"

## Overview

Geostatistical models are increasingly important in public health research
due to the rise in spatial health data. This intensive course suits
statisticians and public health professionals wanting to enhance their
skills in geospatial analysis and modelling. Participants learn about
spatial data structures and geostatistics through real-life examples,
progressing from basic to complex models using Bayesian inference with
the INLA approach. The focus is on spatial patterns of malaria and other
health outcomes, with an emphasis on skills that continue to develop
after the course.

## Who Should Apply

This course is designed for statisticians and public health professionals
who want to build their geospatial analysis and modelling skills.
Candidates should have:

- Basic experience with R
- An understanding of statistical inference
- Introductory knowledge of Bayesian statistical methods

## Format

- **Duration:** typically a three-day intensive training
- **Instructors:** leading experts in geospatial modelling and public
  health
- **Teaching method:** a mix of lectures and hands-on practicals, using
  real-life examples drawn from malaria research
- **Software:** R (version 4.0 and above)
- **Language of instruction:** English

## What You'll Learn

Lecture topics include:

- Introduction to Geostatistics
- Spatial Data in R
- Areal Data and Models
- Geostatistical Models in INLA
- Basics of Point Process Models (where time allows)
